claim: Let \(a_1=1\) and \(a_n=a_{n-1}+\operatorname{lcm}(n,a_{n-1})\) for \(n\ge2\), and put \(b_n=n/\gcd(n,a_{n-1})\). For every prime \(p\ge5\), one has \(b_{2p}\in\{1,p\}\) and, more sharply, \[b_{2p}=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad b_{2p-1}=2p-1.\] Consequently \(b_{2p}=p\) exactly when \(b_{2p-1}\ne2p-1\). If the prime-or-one conjecture is assumed only at the single index \(2p-1\), then this becomes the prime-pair detector \[b_{2p}=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 2p-1\text{ is prime}.\] The forward implication from primality of \(2p-1\) is unconditional. Thus, under the global prime-or-one conjecture, the zero increments at indices \(2p\) with \(p\) prime encode exactly the prime pairs \(p,2p-1\).
integrity: The proof is elementary and infinite. The finite exact-arithmetic replay through n=200000 is used only as a regression check and is explicitly not treated as proof of the conditional prime-pair converse.
scientific_limitations: The unconditional theorem identifies exactly when the even semiprime index has increment one, but the converse from that event to primality of the preceding odd number still requires the prime-or-one conjecture at that single preceding index. No infinitude of the prime pairs is claimed.
title: Exact doubling detector in the LCM prime-increment recurrence
